While the general principles of precipitation hardening and domain wall pinning are textbook knowledge, the specific claims that a low-temperature aging treatment will produce coherent nanoscale precipitates in a high-entropy magnetic alloy and that these will increase coercivity are not supported by any cited experimental results.
premises: Low-temperature aging of a cast high-entropy magnetic alloy can induce nanoscale, coherent precipitates.
These nanoscale, coherent precipitates act as domain wall pinning centers.
Domain wall pinning by precipitates increases the coercive field.
The effect holds under specific aging conditions (temperature/time window) without over-aging.
